desc: Implement forced-character assignment: create array `word` of size n+m-1 initialized to None; for each 'T' index i, write str2 into word[i:i+m], detecting conflicts (return "" on mismatch).
Fill remaining None positions with 'a' and build a boolean array `forced` marking which positions were set by 'T' constraints.
Validate all 'F' windows: detect windows equal to str2 and fix by editing rightmost free position; return "" if a fully-forced F-window matches.

Verify correctness of the iterative F-fix loop: termination, lexicographic minimality of rightmost-free-position edits, and that the while-loop leaves no F-window matching; test the three examples plus edge cases (m=1 with 'F', all 'T's consistent/inconsistent, fully forced F-window, cascading overlaps where one fix creates another match).

Fix the F-fix character choice: use chr(ord(target)+1) instead of 'a'/'b' selection (found termination/minimality bug); add 'z' fallback by scanning leftward for a free position with target < 'z', returning "" if none; re-run all examples and edge cases.

Check complexity is within limits for n=10^4, m=500; replaced full re-scan with a queue of affected F-windows (start indices in [pos-m+1, pos] after editing position pos), with in_queue dedup; re-verified examples.
Stress-test against a brute-force checker for small n, m to confirm minimality and validity of the final implementation.
